mainTopic: רב חסדא and רבא on what רבי עקיבא asked about separate acts: the ברייתות about רבן גמליאל writing on two שבתות, the wording of the נדה proof, and the debate over one חטאת or many.
overview: Writing two letters is the smallest amount of writing that makes someone liable on שבת, so one letter is only a חצי שיעור. Two ברייתות disagree about someone who wrote one letter on each of two שבתות: one says רבן גמליאל holds him חייב, and the other says פטור. רב חסדא and רבא argue about what רבי עקיבא asked רבי אליעזר. רב חסדא says it was about forgetting שבת, and whether the days in between split the sins. רבא says it was about forgetting the מלאכות, and whether separate שבתות count as one unit. Under רבא, the פטור ברייתא seems to have no case, so רבא says רבן גמליאל holds like רבי אליעזר, and the word 'ומודה' is explained through the argument about two half-figs carried into two רשויות. The גמרא then tests both views against the wording of the משנה: נדה or נדות, and 'minor girls'. Finally a ברייתא gives a different version of the debate, in which רבי עקיבא asks about repeated acts with a נדה, and רבי אליעזר's proofs from שבת, minor girls and an animal are each rejected. The פרק ends, and a new משנה begins about cases of doubt in eating חלב.

steps.title: How רב חסדא explains the ברייתא that says liable
steps.stepSummary: According to רב חסדא, the ברייתא that says חייב is talking about someone who forgot it was שבת but knew writing is forbidden. He is liable because there is no awareness for a half-measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the ברייתא that says he is liable is talking about someone who forgot it was שבת but knew the work was forbidden. This holds even though separate שבתות count as separate units. The reason is that he holds there is no awareness for a half-measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב חסדא's way of explaining both ברייתות. It shows which case the ברייתא that says חייב is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the person forgot it was שבת. So when the weekdays came, he could have realized his mistake, and normally that awareness would split the two acts apart. But he only wrote half a measure (one letter) on the first שבת, and awareness does not count for a half-measure. So both letters join together into one act of liability, even though according to רב חסדא, separate שבתות are separate units.

keyTerms.meaning: A mistake about the day: he forgot it was שבת
He knew that this kind of work is forbidden on שבת
They are like separate bodies, meaning separate units
Becoming aware of a mistake does not count when only half the needed amount was done
Liable (here, to bring a חטאת)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of mistakes. In שגגת שבת he forgot what day it was. In שגגת מלאכות he knew it was שבת but did not know the work was forbidden. Each kind leads to a different reason for the ruling.

phrases.english: And that which is taught, "liable":
is where he forgot it was Shabbat but knew the labors were forbidden
(even though Shabbatot are like separate bodies),
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. Either way, he is liable even though רב חסדא treats each שבת as separate.

phrases.english: because he holds: there is no awareness for a half-measure.
phrases.notes: One letter is only half the amount needed to be liable, so realizing the mistake during the week doesn't split the two letters apart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב חסדא's reconciliation, which began before this section, by assigning the ברייתא that says liable to its own case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: אוקימתא: placing the ברייתא in a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If שבתות are separate units, one might think writing on two different שבתות could never combine.
steps.terutzMaskana: When he forgot it was שבת, the letters combine anyway, because awareness does not count for a half-measure.

steps.title: Turning to רבא's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks how the two ברייתות fit with רבא, who holds that separate שבתות count as one unit.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבא, who says that רבי עקיבא holds that separate שבתות are like one unit, how do we explain the two ברייתות?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא switches from רב חסדא to רבא and gets ready to test whether רבא can explain both ברייתות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא could explain both ברייתות because each one had a different reason. רבא holds the opposite basic idea: all the שבתות join into one unit. The question is whether that leaves any room for the ברייתא that says פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: Like one body, meaning one single unit
He holds, he is of the opinion

phrases.english: But according to Rava, who says:
Rabbi Akiva holds
that Shabbatot are like one body,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing רב חסדא, the גמרא applies the same test to רבא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can the two ברייתות be explained according to רבא's view that שבתות are one unit?

steps.title: Granted, the ברייתא that says liable fits רבא
steps.stepSummary: Under רבא, the ברייתא that says חייב works in both kinds of mistake cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is understandable that the ברייתא says he is liable. You can find that in two cases. First, where he knew it was שבת but didn't know the work was forbidden: he is liable because שבתות are one unit. Second, where he forgot it was שבת but knew the work was forbidden: he is liable because there is no awareness for a half-measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא grants that the ברייתא that says חייב is easy to explain under רבא. This is the first half of a challenge, and it sets up the hard part in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case, his mistake was about the work, so the weekdays don't make him aware of anything. The two letters join simply because both שבתות are one unit. In the second case, the weekdays could make him aware, but awareness doesn't count for a half-measure. So under רבא, both kinds of cases lead to חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it is understandable (the first half of a challenge)
You can find it, meaning there is a case where it works
He knew it was שבת
He did not know the work was forbidden

steps.whyThisMatters: By showing that both kinds of cases lead to חייב, the גמרא has used up every possible case. That is exactly what makes the next question so hard.

phrases.english: Granted, that which is taught "liable":
you can find it both where he knew it was Shabbat
but was unaware the labors were forbidden,
because Shabbatot are like one body,
and where he forgot it was Shabbat but knew the labors were forbidden,
because he holds: there is no awareness for a half-measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the setup question by granting the easy half.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that שבתות are one unit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבא, both kinds of cases lead to חייב. That leaves no case for the ברייתא that says פטור.

steps.title: No case fits the ברייתא that says exempt
steps.stepSummary: Under רבא, the ברייתא that says פטור cannot fit either kind of case, so it seems impossible to explain.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא that says he is exempt: what case can you put it in? It doesn't fit this case, and it doesn't fit that case!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes its challenge against רבא. The ברייתא that says פטור has no case left to fit into.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case of knowing it was שבת is already חייב, because the שבתות are one unit. The case of forgetting it was שבת is already חייב, because awareness doesn't count for a half-measure. Since those are the only two cases, the ruling of פטור is left with no case at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt (no חטאת)
In what case can you place it?
Not in this one and not in that one

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב חסדא, each ברייתא fits a different kind of mistake. According to רבא, both kinds of mistakes lead to חייב, so the ברייתא that says פטור has nowhere to go. This is a strong challenge to רבא.

phrases.english: But that which is taught "exempt":
in what case do you place it?
Not in this one and not in that one!
phrases.notes: "This one" and "that one" are the two cases from the last step: knowing it was שבת, and forgetting it was שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא הָדְתַנְיָא פָּטוּר, בְּמַאי מוֹקְמַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the בשלמא structure. The easy half was granted, and now the hard half is pressed.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that רבי עקיבא holds שבתות are one unit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both possible cases already lead to חייב under רבא, so the ברייתא that rules פטור cannot be explained.

steps.title: רבא says רבן גמליאל follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the problem: the פטור ברייתא follows רבן גמליאל, who agrees with רבי אליעזר that separate שבתות are like separate bodies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא could tell you: רבן גמליאל holds like רבי אליעזר, who says that different שבתות are like separate bodies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבא's answer to the problem from Step 4. The ברייתא that says פטור follows the view that different שבתות are counted separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said the פטור ברייתא could not fit רבא's approach. רבא answers that this ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר's idea that each שבת is its own unit, like separate bodies. Because of that, a letter written on one שבת does not join with a letter written on another שבת, so he is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: Different שבתות are like separate bodies, so actions on different שבתות do not join together
He holds (this opinion)

phrases.english: Rava could say to you:

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל סְבִירָא לֵיהּ כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר,
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel holds like Rabbi Eliezer,
who says: Shabbatot are like separate bodies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty raised in Step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ברייתא to a specific תנא (רבן גמליאל, holding like רבי אליעזר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פטור ברייתא cannot be explained at all according to רבא
steps.terutzMaskana: The פטור ברייתא follows רבן גמליאל, who holds like רבי אליעזר that שבתות are like separate bodies

steps.title: The word 'concedes' implies an argument elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that 'ומודה רבן גמליאל' means רבן גמליאל agrees here but argues in some other case.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the ברייתא teaches 'And רבן גמליאל concedes,' this implies that they argue about some other case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a challenge to רבא's answer. It is setting up the next move by noticing a word in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You only say someone 'concedes' if he disagrees somewhere else. So רבן גמליאל must argue with the חכמים in some related case. The next steps will test whether we can find that case under רבא's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: And he agrees (concedes)
By implication
That they argue
About another case

phrases.english: But from the fact that it teaches:
"And Rabban Gamliel concedes,"
it is implied that they disagree about another case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a challenge to רבא's answer in Step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that רבן גמליאל holds like רבי אליעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording 'concedes' requires a related case where רבן גמליאל argues. That case must be identifiable.

steps.title: If he held like רבי עקיבא, the argument would make sense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that if רבן גמליאל held like רבי עקיבא, we could easily find the argument. They would argue in the case of forgetting שבת, and agree in the case of forgetting the מלאכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, if you say he holds like רבי עקיבא, that explains where they argue. They argue when someone forgot it was שבת but knew the labors were forbidden, because רבן גמליאל holds there is no awareness for a half-measure. And רבן גמליאל agrees that if someone knew it was שבת but forgot the labors were forbidden, he is exempt. This shows that שבתות are like separate bodies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how neatly things would work if רבן גמליאל held like רבי עקיבא. This is the 'easy side' of the challenge, and it sets up the contrast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי עקיבא's approach there are two cases. In שגגת שבת וזדון מלאכות, רבן גמליאל says חייב, because a half-measure has no awareness to split it. That is where they argue. In זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות, he agrees it is פטור, because שבתות are like separate bodies. So the word 'concedes' fits perfectly.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this works out fine (introduces the side that has no problem)
Forgetting that it is שבת
Knowing that the acts are forbidden מלאכות
Becoming aware between two half-measures does not split them apart
This shows that

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. 'שגגת שבת וזדון מלאכות' means he forgot it was שבת. 'זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות' means he knew it was שבת but forgot the acts were forbidden. They argue in the first case and agree in the second.

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
he holds like Rabbi Akiva –
that is why they disagree
about forgetting it was Shabbat while knowing the labors are forbidden,
for Rabban Gamliel holds:
there is no awareness for a half-measure.
And Rabban Gamliel concedes
in a case of knowing it is Shabbat but not knowing the labors are forbidden
that he is exempt,
evidently, Shabbatot are like separate bodies.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the required argument can easily be found under the רבי עקיבא approach, to sharpen the challenge
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's choice of רבי אליעזר instead of רבי עקיבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי עקיבא there is a clear case of argument and a clear case of agreement. The contrast prepares the problem for the רבי אליעזר approach.

steps.title: With רבי אליעזר, where would they argue?
steps.stepSummary: If רבן גמליאל holds like רבי אליעזר, the word 'concedes' still means they argue somewhere. The גמרא asks: about what?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say רבן גמליאל holds like רבי אליעזר, it is implied that they disagree. About what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבא's actual answer and asks which case the argument could be about. This sets up the attack in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'concedes' still requires a case where they argue. Under רבי אליעזר's approach, the גמרא now has to find that case. The question 'במאי' opens the search.

keyTerms.meaning: But (here, introducing the side that has a problem)
About what?

phrases.english: But if you say

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סְבִירָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel holds like Rabbi Eliezer,
it is implied that they disagree.
About what?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with Step 7 by applying the same test to רבא's approach
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case רבן גמליאל and the חכמים argue about, if רבן גמליאל holds like רבי אליעזר

steps.title: רבי אליעזר also holds there is no awareness for a half-measure
steps.stepSummary: They cannot argue about forgetting שבת, because רבי אליעזר also holds there is no awareness for a half-measure. A ברייתא shows he makes the person חייב for two letters written on two שבתות.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they argue about forgetting שבת while knowing the labors, that doesn't work. Even רבי אליעזר agrees with רבן גמליאל that there is no awareness for a half-measure. As it is taught: One who writes two letters on two שבתות, one letter on this שבת and one letter on that שבת, רבי אליעזר holds him liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the obvious place for the argument and shows it fails. In that case רבי אליעזר agrees with רבן גמליאל, so there is nothing to argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי עקיבא, the argument was in the case of שגגת שבת וזדון מלאכות. But a ברייתא says רבי אליעזר makes someone חייב for one letter on each of two שבתות. So רבי אליעזר also holds there is no awareness for a half-measure, and that case cannot be the argument. This weakens רבא's claim that רבן גמליאל holds like רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Even
Letters (writing two letters is the minimum for the מלאכה of writing)
Holds him liable

phrases.english: If they disagree about forgetting it was Shabbat while knowing the labors are forbidden –

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
phrases.english: even Rabbi Eliezer holds like Rabban Gamliel
that there is no awareness for a half-measure,
as it is taught in a baraita:
One who writes two letters on two Shabbatot,
one letter on this Shabbat
and one letter on that Shabbat –
Rabbi Eliezer holds him liable!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בְּשִׁגְגַת שַׁבָּת וּזְדוֹן מְלָאכוֹת אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to Step 8's question and rejects it
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that, under רבי אליעזר, the argument could be in the case of שגגת שבת וזדון מלאכות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows רבי אליעזר also holds there is no awareness for a half-measure. So רבן גמליאל and the חכמים (following רבי אליעזר) would agree in that case, and there is no argument left.

steps.title: Maybe they argue about adding one thread to woven cloth? No
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר argue about adding a single thread to an existing woven fabric. It rejects the idea, because a משנה shows רבי אליעזר also makes that person חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, perhaps they argue about adding one thread to a woven fabric? But רבי אליעזר holds that person חייב! As we learned: רבי אליעזר says, one who weaves three threads at the start, or one thread onto a woven fabric, is חייב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second possible case where the two תנאים might argue, and then knocks it down right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea was that רבן גמליאל holds the person חייב for adding one thread, while רבי אליעזר holds him פטור. But a משנה quotes רבי אליעזר himself saying the person is חייב. So they agree here, and this cannot be the hidden argument behind 'ומודה'.

keyTerms.meaning: A fabric that is already woven
Threads
He actually holds the person liable
At the beginning, when starting a new fabric

phrases.english: But rather, [perhaps they argue] about one [thread] onto a woven fabric?
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves out the word 'thread' here, but the משנה quoted next makes it clear.

phrases.english: [But רבי אליעזר] does hold him liable,
as we learned: Rabbi Eliezer says:
One who weaves three threads at the beginning,
or one onto a woven fabric, is liable!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא, בְּאַחַת עַל הָאָרִיג – חַיּוֹבֵי מְחַיֵּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 9 ruled out forgetting שבת, this step tries and rules out a second possible case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the argument behind 'ומודה' is about adding one thread to woven cloth
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה shows רבי אליעזר holds the person חייב in this case, so there is no argument here.

steps.title: רבא finds the argument: two halves of a fig
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the case where רבן גמליאל argues is the ברייתא about carrying out two half-figs. In that ברייתא, the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי disagree about whether two separate רשויות split the act.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Since 'concedes' implies he argues about one thing, it is this, as a ברייתא teaches. If someone carried out half a dried fig and then carried out another half, in one העלם, he is חייב. In two העלמות, he is פטור. רבי יוסי says: in one העלם and into one רשות, he is חייב. Into two רשויות, he is פטור.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question from step 8. He brings a ברייתא with a real argument that can be the case where רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that two half-measures done in one העלם combine to a full measure. The argument is about two separate רשויות. The תנא קמא says the halves still combine. רבי יוסי says the separate רשויות split them apart, so the person is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication; from what the words suggest
A dried fig, the minimum amount for carrying on שבת
A period of forgetting or unawareness
A domain, such as a separate public area
Exempt; he does not bring a חטאת

steps.whatToRemember: Two halves combine in one העלם. The only argument is whether two separate רשויות split them: the תנא קמא says no, רבי יוסי says yes.

phrases.english: Rava said: Since it is implied that he argues about one thing,
phrases.notes: He means the word 'ומודה' tells us רבן גמליאל argues somewhere, and רבא is now saying where.

phrases.english: as it is taught: If he carried out half a dried fig,
and then went back and carried out another half a dried fig,
in one lapse of awareness, he is liable.
phrases.notes: Some versions say אחת, and the corrected wording in square brackets says אחד. The meaning is the same.

phrases.english: In two lapses of awareness, he is exempt.
Rabbi Yosei says: In one lapse of awareness,
into one domain, he is liable,
into two domains, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After two cases were rejected (steps 9 and 10), רבא supplies the real case of disagreement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a different case where the two תנאים argue
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed there was no case left where רבן גמליאל could argue with רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: They argue about two half-measures carried into two separate רשויות.

steps.title: Matching each תנא to a side of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל holds like the תנא קמא: separate רשויות do not split the act. רבי אליעזר holds like רבי יוסי: separate רשויות do split it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל holds like the תנא קמא, and רבי אליעזר holds like רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his answer by placing רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר on the two sides of the half-fig argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So רבן גמליאל does not split an act because of separate רשויות. But he 'concedes' that separate שבתות do split it, so two letters written on two שבתות leave the person פטור. This solves the question of what 'ומודה' was pointing to.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the ברייתא's word 'ומודה' a real meaning. It also keeps רבא's answer from step 5 standing: the פטור ruling follows רבן גמליאל.

phrases.english: For Rabban Gamliel holds like the first tanna,
and Rabbi Eliezer holds like Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא from step 11 to the two תנאים in question.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבן גמליאל argues with רבי אליעזר about separate רשויות but agrees that separate שבתות split the act.

steps.title: A new proof begins: רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר from נדה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new proof from the משנה. רבי אליעזר tells רבי עקיבא that the person is חייב for each מלאכה, based on a קל וחומר from נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: he said to him, 'He is חייב for each and every one, from a קל וחומר. If נדה, which does not have many results…'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof from the משנה by quoting the start of רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר. The next step shows that its wording, נדה, fits רב חסדא better than רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי אליעזר argues that if separate acts with a נדה each bring their own חטאת, even though נדה has few kinds of acts, then שבת should surely work the same way. The גמרא quotes only the opening words, because the next step focuses on the exact word נדה (one woman) to test רב חסדא's and רבא's explanations.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'how much more so' argument, from a lighter case to a stronger one
A woman in her niddah period; relations with her are forbidden
Results or offshoots, here meaning different kinds of forbidden acts
Each and every one

phrases.english: Come and hear: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבי אליעזר speaking to רבי עקיבא in the משנה.

phrases.english: He is liable for each and every one
phrases.notes: He means each מלאכה done on שבת.

phrases.english: from an a fortiori argument,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה נִדָּה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ תּוֹצָאוֹת הַרְבֵּה.
phrases.english: If a niddah, which does not have many results…

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, אָמַר לוֹ: חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ומודה discussion is settled, the גמרא brings a proof from the משנה's wording to decide between רב חסדא and רבא.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's reading of רבי עקיבא's question (whether the days in between count as awareness), which fits רבי אליעזר's comparison to a single נדה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר from נדה in the משנה

steps.title: The singular word נדה fits רב חסדא but not רבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר's word "נדה" (one woman) suits רב חסדא's explanation, which is about the days in between. For רבא's explanation, which is about שבתות being like separate bodies, the משנה should have said "נדות" (many women).
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for רב חסדא, who says רבי עקיבא's question was about someone who forgot it was שבת but knew the מלאכות were forbidden. His question was whether the days in between count as awareness that splits the sins. That is why רבי אליעזר answered "and just as with a נדה." But for רבא, who says the question was about someone who knew it was שבת but did not know the מלאכות were forbidden, the question was whether separate שבתות are like separate bodies. Then the answer should have said "נדות"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the exact word רבי אליעזר used and finds that it fits רב חסדא but seems to go against רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב חסדא, the question is about days passing between the sins, so one נדה with time between each act is the right comparison. For רבא, the question is whether each שבת counts as a separate 'body'. The matching comparison would be many different women, נדות, so the singular word challenges רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: He forgot it was שבת, but he knew the acts were forbidden מלאכות
He knew it was שבת, but he did not know the acts were forbidden
The days in between the sins
Awareness that splits the sins into separate sin-offerings
Like separate bodies (separate objects of sin)
One woman who is a נדה / many such women

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. רב חסדא's person forgot it was שבת. רבא's person knew it was שבת but did not know the acts were forbidden.

phrases.english: It works well for Rav Chisda, who says:

phrases.aramaic: שִׁגְגַת שַׁבָּת וּזְדוֹן מְלָאכוֹת בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: he (רבי עקיבא) asked him about forgetting שבת while knowing the מלאכות were forbidden,
whether the days in between are
awareness that splits the sins or not –
that is why he said to him: "And just as with a נדה."
phrases.notes: This is רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר from the משנה, which we saw in Step 13.

phrases.english: But for Rava, who says:
about knowing it was שבת but not knowing the מלאכות were forbidden
is what he asked him,

phrases.aramaic: דְּשַׁבָּתוֹת אִי כְּגוּפִין דָּמְיָין וְאִי לָא –
phrases.english: whether Shabbatot are like separate bodies or not –
let it teach "נדות" (many women)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the קל וחומר from נדה, quoted in Step 13, to test the two explanations.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's explanation of רבי עקיבא's question
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the question were about separate bodies, the matching comparison would be many women (נדות), not one woman (נדה).

steps.title: רבא reads the משנה as נדות
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the משנה really should read "נדות".
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא can tell you: read it as "נדות".
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by fixing the wording of the משנה: the correct reading is the plural.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of explaining away the singular word, רבא says the correct version of the משנה says "נדות". With that reading, רבי אליעזר's comparison matches the 'separate bodies' idea exactly.

phrases.english: Rava can say to you: read it as "נדות".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבא from Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Corrects the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה says נדה, which fits only רב חסדא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה should read נדות, which fits רבא.

steps.title: Which sages read נדה and which read נדות
steps.stepSummary: שמואל and רב אדא בר אהבה read the משנה as "נדה". רב נתן בר אושעיא reads it as "נדות".
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל teaches "נדה". רב אדא בר אהבה teaches "נדה". רב נתן בר אושעיא says: teach "נדות".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that the sages had two versions of the משנה's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that רבא's reading is not just made up to save his view. A real version, taught by רב נתן בר אושעיא, says נדות. Still, two other sages kept the singular נדה.

phrases.english: Shmuel teaches "נדה",
Rav Adda bar Ahava teaches "נדה".

phrases.aramaic: רַב נָתָן בַּר אוֹשַׁעְיָא אָמַר: תָּנֵי ״נִדּוֹת״.
phrases.english: Rav Natan bar Oshaya says: teach "נדות".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the reading רבא needs actually existed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two traditions about the wording: נדה (שמואל, רב אדא בר אהבה) and נדות (רב נתן בר אושעיא).

steps.title: For רב חסדא, what days in between does a נדה have?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now challenges רב חסדא. In the case of a נדה, what 'days in between' could count as awareness that splits the sins?
steps.simpleTranslation: And for רב חסדא, who says the question was about forgetting שבת while knowing the מלאכות were forbidden, the question was whether the days in between count as awareness that splits the sins. But with a נדה, what days in between that count as awareness does she have?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the challenge around. Now it asks how רבי אליעזר's comparison to נדה could even fit רב חסדא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's question is about days in between acting as awareness. For the proof from נדה to work, a נדה would need a similar 'days in between' factor. The גמרא asks what that could be, since nothing obvious in her case seems to make him aware of his sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Does she have (is there such a thing in her case)

phrases.english: And for Rav Chisda, who says:
about forgetting שבת while knowing the מלאכות were forbidden
is what he asked him,
whether the days in between are
awareness that splits the sins or not,
a נדה – what days in between
that count as awareness to split the sins does she have?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רבא's side is settled, the גמרא challenges רב חסדא's side of the comparison.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's explanation of רבי עקיבא's question
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The comparison to נדה only helps רב חסדא if a נדה also has days in between that count as awareness, and none seem to exist.

steps.title: Immersions count like the days in between
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a case of a נדה that has 'days in between': she immerses between each act of relations, and each immersion works like a gap of awareness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Picture a case where he had relations with her and then she immersed. Then she saw blood again and he had relations with her again. Then she immersed, and he had relations with her again. The immersions are like the days in between.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question from Step 17. He shows how even with one נדה there can be something like 'days in between' that could split the sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that with a נדה there seem to be no 'days in between' like the weekdays between שבתות. רבא says each immersion (טבילה) ends one period of being forbidden, and a new period starts when she sees blood again. So the immersions play the same role as the weekdays between one שבת and the next. This keeps רב חסדא's reading of the משנה working.

keyTerms.meaning: Immersion in a מקוה, which makes a נדה pure again
The days in between, the gaps that might count as awareness and split the sins
For example, such as; it introduces a sample case
And he went back and did it again

phrases.english: Rava said: For example, where he had relations with her
and she immersed, and she saw blood again
and he again had relations with her, and she immersed,
and he again had relations with her,
phrases.notes: The text doesn't repeat it, but she has seen blood again here, so she is a נדה once more.

phrases.english: for the immersions are like the days in between.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כְּגוֹן שֶׁבָּא עָלֶיהָ וְטָבְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 17 by describing a case where 'days in between' exist for a נדה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case limitation: it sets up a specific case with repeated immersions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A single נדה has no gaps that could act like the days between Shabbatot, so רב חסדא's reading fails.
steps.terutzMaskana: The immersions between each act of relations work like the days in between, so רב חסדא's reading holds.

steps.title: The word 'minor girls' fits רבא's reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר's line 'one who has relations with minor girls will prove it.' The plural 'girls' fits רבא well.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'One who has relations with minor girls will prove it.' This works well for רבא, because that is why it says 'minor girls' in the plural.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another line from the משנה to support רבא. This also sets up a challenge to רב חסדא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא says the question was whether separate שבתות are like separate 'bodies.' Several different girls are clearly separate bodies, so the plural 'minor girls' matches his view exactly. The next steps ask how רב חסדא, who talks about one woman and the days in between, explains the plural, and step 21 answers.

keyTerms.meaning: Minor girls; here written in the plural
Will prove it; a case brought to break the other side's argument
It works well for...; this sets up a contrast with another opinion

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: הַבָּא עַל הַקְּטַנּוֹת יוֹכִיחַ.
phrases.english: Come and hear: One who has relations with minor girls will prove it.
phrases.notes: These are רבי אליעזר's words to רבי עקיבא, later in the same משנה.

phrases.english: It works well according to Rava,
this is why it teaches 'minor girls' in the plural.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הַבָּא עַל הַקְּטַנּוֹת יוֹכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the wording debate from Steps 14-15 (נדה versus נדות), now using the word קטנות.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's reading, that the question was about Shabbatot being separate 'bodies'
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אליעזר's words in the משנה: 'הַבָּא עַל הַקְּטַנּוֹת יוֹכִיחַ', which use the plural

steps.title: Why the plural according to רב חסדא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב חסדא, who speaks about one woman, explains the plural 'minor girls.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רב חסדא, what does 'minor girls' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא. If the case is about one woman and the days in between, why does the משנה use a plural word?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's reading needs only one woman. Several separate acts with her are split by the gaps in between. A plural word seems to point toward several women, which is רבא's idea. So the wording seems to work against רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: But; it turns to the other opinion that has a problem
What? Here it asks what the word means

phrases.english: But according to Rav Chisda,
what is meant by 'minor girls'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the support for רבא in Step 19 into a challenge against רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's explanation of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plural 'minor girls' suggests several women, but רב חסדא's reading is about one woman with gaps in between.

steps.title: Minor girls in general
steps.stepSummary: The answer for רב חסדא: the plural just describes minor girls in general. It does not mean one man with several girls.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means minor girls in general.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב חסדא. The plural is only a general way of speaking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural refers to the general category: whenever any man has relations with a minor girl. It does not describe one man with many girls. So each case can still be one man and one girl, which fits רב חסדא's 'days in between' approach.

keyTerms.meaning: In general; of the world at large

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'קטנות דעלמא' as saying the man was with many girls. It means the opposite: the plural is just a general way of describing the type of case.

phrases.english: Minor girls in general.
phrases.notes: Meaning: any man with any minor girl, not one man with several girls.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording: the plural is general, not a description of several women
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The plural 'minor girls' means one man with several girls, which would only fit רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The plural speaks of minor girls in general, so it fits רב חסדא too.

steps.title: A different version of רבי עקיבא's question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה does not match a ברייתא. In that ברייתא, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says רבי עקיבא really asked about a man who had relations several times with his wife while she was a נדה, all in one lapse of awareness.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not like that תנא. A ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said, that is not what רבי עקיבא asked רבי אליעזר. This is what he asked him: If a man had relations with his wife while she was a נדה, and then again had relations with his wife while she was a נדה, all in one lapse of awareness, what is the law? Is he liable once for all of them, or for each one separately?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new point. It brings a ברייתא with a different version of what רבי עקיבא asked, and says the משנה does not follow it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי עקיבא's question is about שבת, and רבי אליעזר answers from נדה. In רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's version, the question itself is about a נדה: repeated acts with the same wife, all forgotten together (העלם אחד). The question is whether he brings one offering for all of them or one for each.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage of the משנה period; here, the one whose version differs from the משנה
One lapse of awareness; he forgot the prohibition the whole time
Liable only once for all the acts together
For each and every one separately

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the exchange between רבי עקיבא and רבי אליעזר was passed down in two versions: one about שבת, and one about a נדה directly.

phrases.english: This is not like this תנא, as it is taught:
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא כָּךְ שְׁאֵלוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר,
phrases.english: That is not what Rabbi Akiva asked Rabbi Elazar,
phrases.notes: This is the same sage from the משנה, רבי אליעזר; the name is just spelled differently here.

phrases.english: rather, this is what he asked him:
One who had relations with his wife while she was a נדה
and again had relations with his wife while she was a נדה
in one lapse of awareness, what is the law?
Is he liable once for all of them,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת?
phrases.english: or is he liable for each and every one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the רבא and רב חסדא discussion ends, the גמרא brings a ברייתא with a different version of the exchange quoted in Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, רבי עקיבא asked about repeated relations with a wife who is a נדה in one lapse of awareness: is he liable once, or for each act?

steps.title: רבי אליעזר proves from שבת that each act needs its own offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר rules that the man brings a separate חטאת for each act of relations with a נדה. He proves it with a קל וחומר: שבת has only one prohibition and still creates many obligations, so נדה, which has two prohibitions, should certainly do the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: He is liable for each and every one, from a קל וחומר. שבת has only one prohibition: he is warned about שבת, but שבת is not warned about him. Yet he is liable for each and every one. A נדה has two prohibitions: he is warned about her, and she is warned about him. Isn't it logical that he is liable for each and every one?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers רבי עקיבא's question from the ברייתא. He says the man brings a separate חטאת for every act, and he uses a קל וחומר from שבת to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With שבת, only the person is commanded, and still one lapse can produce many separate חטאות. With נדה, both people are commanded, so the איסור is 'double.' רבי אליעזר argues that the stricter case (נדה) must be at least as strict as the lighter case (שבת).

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stricter one: if the light case has this rule, the strict case surely does too
A Torah warning, meaning a prohibition
Warned, meaning commanded not to do something
Each and every one, meaning a separate liability for every act
Is it not logical? The standard way to finish a קל וחומר

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבי אליעזר answering רבי עקיבא's question from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: He is liable for each and every one,
from an a fortiori argument:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה שַׁבָּת שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ אֶלָּא אַזְהָרָה אַחַת,
phrases.english: Just as Shabbat, which has only one prohibition,
since he is warned about Shabbat
but Shabbat is not warned about him,
he is liable for each and every one,
then with a menstruating woman, who has two prohibitions,
since he is warned about the menstruating woman
and the menstruating woman is warned about him,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת?
phrases.english: is it not logical that he is liable for each and every one?

steps.triggerLanguage: חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת, מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question רבי עקיבא asked in the ברייתא quoted in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: A man brings a separate חטאת for each act of relations with a נדה done in one lapse of awareness.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from שבת, which has only one prohibition and still creates many separate liabilities.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: שבת has many separate kinds of sin, but נדה does not
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא breaks the קל וחומר. שבת is different because it contains many different kinds of forbidden acts, and each kind brings its own חטאת. נדה has only one kind of act.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: No. You can say this about שבת, which has many separate categories that lead to many חטאות. Can you say it about נדה, which does not have many categories leading to many חטאות?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא rejects רבי אליעזר's proof from שבת by showing that שבת has a special feature that נדה lacks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The many חטאות of שבת come from its many different categories of forbidden work. That is the real reason for the many liabilities, not how strict the איסור is. Since נדה has only one forbidden act, the קל וחומר falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: No, if you said... The standard opening for breaking a קל וחומר
Outcomes or branches, here meaning separate categories of forbidden acts
Sin offerings brought for doing a forbidden act by mistake

phrases.english: They said to him:
phrases.notes: The wording is plural, but in this ברייתא it is רבי עקיבא answering.

phrases.english: No, if you said this about Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ תּוֹצָאוֹת הַרְבֵּה לְחַטָּאוֹת הַרְבֵּה,
phrases.english: which has many categories that lead to many sin offerings,
will you say it about the menstruating woman,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ תּוֹצָאוֹת הַרְבֵּה לְחַטָּאוֹת הַרְבֵּה!
phrases.english: which does not have many categories that lead to many sin offerings!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Breaks the קל וחומר from step 23.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שבת's many liabilities come from its many categories of forbidden work, a feature נדה does not have.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר brings the case of minor girls as proof
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers that the case of a man who has relations with several minor girls who are נדות proves his point. There is only one kind of act there too, yet he is liable separately for each girl.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: One who has relations with minor girls will prove it. There are not many categories leading to many חטאות there, and still he is liable for each and every one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר brings a new case to show that many חטאות can come even when there is only one kind of forbidden act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא said many חטאות need many different categories. רבי אליעזר shows a case with just one category, relations with a נדה, that still brings a separate חטאת for each girl. So one category alone does not limit the liability to one offering.

keyTerms.meaning: Will prove it, meaning this case shows the point is true
Minor girls, here girls who are נדות
One who has relations with

phrases.english: They said to him:
phrases.notes: Here it is רבי אליעזר answering back.

phrases.english: One who has relations with minor girls will prove it,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ תּוֹצָאוֹת הַרְבֵּה לְחַטָּאוֹת הַרְבֵּה,
phrases.english: for it does not have many categories that lead to many sin offerings,
and yet he is liable for each and every one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי עקיבא's rejection in step 24 with a counter-example.
steps.raayaObject: One kind of forbidden act can still bring many חטאות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of one who has relations with several minor girls who are נדות.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the minor girls are separate people
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא rejects the proof. With the minor girls, each act involves a different person, so of course each one counts separately. A man with his one wife is a different case.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: No. You can say this about minor girls, because they are separate bodies.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא pushes back on the minor girls case by pointing out what makes it different from the case he asked about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With several girls, the separate people are what split the liability into many חטאות. In רבי עקיבא's question it is one wife, one body, many times. So the girls do not prove anything about his case.

keyTerms.meaning: Separate bodies, meaning different people who each count on their own
Since, because. It points out the feature that makes the case different

phrases.english: They said to him:
No, if you said this about minor girls,
that is because they are separate bodies!
phrases.notes: The unspoken rest of the line: will you say the same about one wife many times?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא, אִם אָמַרְתָּ בַּקְּטַנּוֹת שֶׁכֵּן גּוּפִין מוּחְלָקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the minor girls proof from step 25.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Each girl is a separate person, while רבי עקיבא's question is about one woman.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר brings the case of an animal as proof
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר brings a case with no separate bodies: a man who sins with one animal many times. He claims the man is liable for each act.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: One who has relations with an animal will prove it. There are no separate bodies there, and still he is liable for each and every one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר tries again with a case that has no 'separate bodies,' to answer רבי עקיבא's last objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא said separate people are what create many חטאות. רבי אליעזר claims that with one animal, which is one body, the man is still liable for each act. If so, many acts with one body can bring many offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal
There are no separate bodies, meaning it is the same one body each time

phrases.english: They said to him:
One who has relations with an animal will prove it,
for there are no separate bodies,
and yet he is liable for each and every one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'separate bodies' objection of step 26 with a new example.
steps.raayaObject: Many acts with one body bring a separate חטאת for each act.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of one who sins many times with an animal.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the animal is just like the נדה
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא does not accept that the animal case is settled. He says the animal is the same as the נדה: many acts in one lapse bring only one חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: The animal is like the נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers that the animal case proves nothing, because he holds the same rule there. The debate ends here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A proof only works if the other side agrees with the case being used. רבי עקיבא does not agree. In his view, the man who sins with an animal many times in one lapse also brings only one חטאת, just like with the נדה.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the נדה, meaning it follows the same rule

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר: separate חטאת for each act with a נדה. רבי עקיבא: one חטאת for many acts in one lapse with the same body. Each proof failed for its own reason: שבת has many categories, the minor girls are separate people, and רבי עקיבא holds the animal case works just like נדה.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי עקיבא agrees about the animal and just found a difference. He disagrees with the case itself: for him, the animal also brings only one חטאת.

phrases.english: They said to him:
The animal is like the menstruating woman.
phrases.notes: He means the man brings only one offering for the animal as well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the animal proof from step 27 by refusing to accept its premise.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי עקיבא does not accept the premise. For him, many acts with an animal in one lapse also bring only one חטאת.

steps.title: הדרן: Closing the פרק אמרו לו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא formally ends the פרק called אמרו לו.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק אמרו לו.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line of the פרק. It marks the end of the long debate between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא that we just finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new argument is made here. The הדרן is a traditional farewell said at the end of every פרק, and it shows that the topic of that פרק is now finished. The פרק is called אמרו לו after its opening words.

keyTerms.meaning: "We will return to you": the formula said when finishing a perek

steps.whatToRemember: The פרק אמרו לו ends with the unresolved debate about one act versus many acts in a single lapse. A new topic, doubt, begins next.

phrases.english: We will return to you, "They said to him"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the perek right after רבי עקיבא's final rejection in step 28.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The perek אמרו לו is complete.

steps.title: New משנה: Cases of doubt about eating forbidden fat
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה starts listing cases where a person is unsure about his sin: whether he ate חלב at all, or whether he ate a full שיעור.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If it is uncertain whether he ate forbidden fat or did not eat it, or even if he did eat it but it is uncertain whether it had the minimum amount, and uncertain...
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק opens with a משנה about doubtful sins. Here it only sets up the cases, and the sentence continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous פרק dealt with sins a person knows he did. Now the topic moves to doubt. The משנה gives two levels of doubt. In the first, he is not sure he ate חלב at all. In the second, he surely ate it but is not sure the piece was big enough to make him liable. The word "even" (ואפילו) tells us the second case also counts as a doubt case.

keyTerms.meaning: "Our משנה": marks the start of the משנה text
Doubt or uncertainty
Forbidden fat of certain animals. Eating it on purpose is punished with כרת, and eating it by mistake requires a חטאת.
The minimum required amount (a כזית) that makes one liable

steps.confusionAlert: "Even if he ate" does not mean he is now certainly liable. He ate חלב for sure, but the doubt is about the size, so this is still a case of doubt.

phrases.english: MISHNA: If it is uncertain whether he ate forbidden fat,
or uncertain whether he did not eat it,
or even if he did eat it,
but it is uncertain whether there is the minimum measure in it
and uncertain

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ סָפֵק אָכַל חֵלֶב, סָפֵק לֹא אָכַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a brand-new perek after the הדרן in step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה sets up cases of doubt: doubt whether חלב was eaten, and doubt whether a full שיעור was eaten. The ruling comes later in the משנה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה opens the discussion of how the Torah treats a person who may have sinned but is not sure. The whole new perek is built on that question.
